title: Word formation: prefixes, suffixes and families
tagline: One root word, many forms: add a suffix for a noun or adjective, a prefix to make it negative.
why: One root word can give you a whole word family — succeed, success, successful, successfully — and B1 Preliminary Reading tests exactly this skill: choosing the right form of a word to fit the sentence. Knowing your suffixes and prefixes also means a much bigger active vocabulary for Writing, without learning a single new root.

hook.text: Nadia is nervous backstage. "What if I'm not successful?" Sofia: "You'll be great — your performance was amazing in rehearsal!" Nadia: "I feel so nervous, it's unbelievable." Sofia: "That's completely normal — everyone feels that way."
hook.ask: Successful, performance and unbelievable all come from smaller root words: succeed, perform and believe. What did English add to each root — and what does un- do to the meaning of believable?

diagrams.title: Building a word family

rules.rule: adjective → negative adjective: un- / dis- / im- / in- / ir-

diagrams.caption: The suffix at the end usually decides the word class; the prefix at the start usually flips the meaning.

diagrams.title: How to choose the right word form

steps.label: Find the gap and decide: noun, verb, adjective or adverb?
Check what comes before/after the gap for clues
Add the right suffix to the root word
Check if you also need a negative prefix

examples.text: Nadia felt a lot of nervousness before going on.
Liam wants to be a musician when he's older.
examples.note: music (noun) + ian → a person who does it

examples.text: The teacher gave us useful advice about the audition.
examples.note: advise (verb) becomes the noun advice — an irregular spelling change

examples.text: That was a pointless argument — nobody won.
Mateo was unhappy with his mark at first.
It's impossible to learn a whole song in one day.
That's a very irresponsible thing to do.

use.point: re-, over-, under- and spelling changes

examples.text: Nadia had to rewrite the lyrics after the first draft.
Liam felt overconfident before the audition, and it showed.

watch_out.why: The noun from perform is performance, not performation — check the exact suffix, not just add -tion to everything.

watch_out.wrong: It was a very successfully film.
watch_out.why: Adjectives use -ful, not the adverb ending -ly, after very and before a noun.
After a verb, you usually need the adverb (-ly form), not the adjective.
The prefix before p, m or b changes to im-, not in-.
responsible takes ir-, not un-, because it starts with r.

watch_out.wrong: The teacher gave us a useful advise.
watch_out.why: advice is the noun, spelled with c; advise is the verb, spelled with s.

l1.why: Spanish -ación often becomes -ation in English, but perform's noun is the irregular performance, not performation.
Spanish always uses im- before p, just like English — but the double s in English (possible) is easy to forget.
Spanish irresponsable and English irresponsible both use ir-; don't swap it for the more common un-.
Spanish consejo is one word, but English splits it: advice (noun, with c) and advise (verb, with s).

remember.trick: One root, four jobs: noun, verb, adjective, adverb!
remember.tip: Learn a whole word family together, not one word at a time: success, succeed, successful, successfully.

dialogue.title: Backstage nerves
dialogue.context: Nadia is about to audition for the school talent show and Sofia, Liam and Mateo help calm her nerves backstage.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: You'll be great, Nadia — your performance in rehearsal was amazing!

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I just feel so much nervousness, I can hardly breathe.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: That's completely normal. Everyone feels hopeful and terrified at the same time.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: It would be impossible not to be nervous before something this big.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: What if my singing isn't enjoyable to listen to?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: It's really impressive, trust me. You sang it beautifully yesterday.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Don't be unhappy about small mistakes — the judges want to see confidence.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Just don't be overconfident either — a bit of nerves helps too.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: OK, I think I'm ready. Wish me success!

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: You'll be successful, I'm sure of it. Go!

can_do: I can build nouns from verbs and adjectives with -tion, -ment, -ness, -er and -ist.
I can build adjectives with -ful, -less, -able, -ive and -ous, and adverbs with -ly.
I can choose the right negative prefix: un-, dis-, im-, in- or ir-.
summary: A word family shares one root but changes form: succeed (verb), success (noun), successful (adjective), successfully (adverb).
Noun suffixes: -tion, -ment, -ness, -er, -ist. Adjective suffixes: -ful, -less, -able, -ive, -ous. Adverbs: add -ly.
Negative prefixes depend on the first letter: im- before m/p/b, ir- before r, il- before l, un- and dis- elsewhere.
re- = do again; over- = too much; under- = not enough.
Watch the spelling changes: happy → happiness (y→i), advise (verb) → advice (noun).
